prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has taken the courses Fundamentals of Chemical Processes, Basic Operations I and II, Kinetics and Chemical Reactors, and Chemical Thermodynamics applied to Engineering.

It is important that the student has the knowledge to formulate and solve material and energy balances, and knows the fundamentals of the functioning of unit operations equipment in Chemical Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.

Knowledge about material and energy balances, biotechnology, mass transfer, separation operations, chemical reaction engineering, reactor design, and valorization and transformation of raw materials and energy resources.
Ability for the analysis, design, simulation and optimization of processes and products.

Ability to design and manage applied experimentation procedures, especially for the determination of thermodynamic and transport properties, and modeling of phenomena and systems in the field of chemical engineering, systems with fluid flow, heat transmission, mass transfer operations, chemical reaction kinetics and reactors.
Ability to design, manage and operate simulation, control and instrumentation procedures for chemical processes.
Know the main chemical processes currently carried out in the industry.
Know the characteristics of the main equipment used in the chemical industry (reactors, separation equipment, heat exchangers etc…).
Know the main environmental implications of industrial chemical processes.
Perform material and energy balances of industrial chemical processes.

syllabus_topics: Tema 2. Energía en la industria química.
Tema 3. Materias primas en la industria química.
Tema 4. El agua como materia prima.
Tema 5. El aire como materia prima.
Tema 9. Amoniaco, ácido nítrico y derivados.
Tema 11. Caliza, derivados y cemento. Yeso.
Tema 18. El animal como fuente de materia prima.
Tema 20. La seguridad y la higiene en la industria química.

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of Classroom Practices and Group Tutorials

assessment_rules: To pass the course, the final evaluation cannot be less than 40% of its maximum value. For the written exam, a minimum of 30% of the theoretical-practical part and 30% of the problem-solving part is required. If the condition for the final evaluation is met, the final grade will be calculated using the specified weighting percentages. For students taking extraordinary calls before the semester the course is typically taught, the final grade will be calculated using the Group Tutorial grade from the immediately preceding academic year and the grade from the extraordinary final evaluation, applying the stated percentages. For differentiated evaluation, the final exam accounts for 100% of the final grade.
